WineD3D is a translation layer for DirectX 1-11 to OpenGL.

DXVK is a translation layer for Direct3D 9-11 to Vulkan.

VKD3D is a translation layer for Direct3D 12 API to Vulkan.

CNC DDraw is an implementation of DirectDraw for better compatibility with classic games.

Handling of flags on CALL/RET opcodes

0 : Treats CALL/RET as if it never needed flags (faster, unstable)
1 : Most RET will need flags, most CALLS will not
2 : All CALL/RET will need flags (slower)
Use of Float/Double for x87 emulation

Dynarec building BigBlock

0 : Don\'t try to build block as big as possible
1 : Build Dynarec block as big as possible
2 : Build Dynarec block bigger (continue when block overlaps, but only for blocks in elf memory)
3 : Build Dynarec block bigger (continue when block overlaps, for all types of memory)

Simulation of Strong Memory model

0 : Don\'t try anything special
1 : Enable some Memory Barrier when writing to memory (on some MOV opcode)
2 : All 1 plus a Memory Barrier on every write to memory using MOV
3 : All 2 plus Memory Barrier when reading from memory and on some SSE/SSE2 opcodes
Defines the max allowed forward value when building Block
Defines whether or not Dynarec will wait for the FillBlock to be ready

Tweak memory barriers to reduce performance impact of strong memory emulation

0 : Use regular safe barriers
1 : Use weak barriers for mild performance boost
2 : Use weak barriers, additionally disable last write barriers

Generate aligned atomics only (only available on Arm64 for now).

0 : Generate unaligned atomics handling code.
1 : Generate aligned atomics only, which is faster and smaller code size, but will cause SIGBUS for LOCK prefixed opcodes operating on aligned data addresses.

Enable or disable the use of deferred flags.

0 : Disable the use of deferred flags.
1 : Enable the use of deferred flags.

Allow continue running a block that is unprotected and potentially dirty.

0 : Do not allow continue running a block that is unprotected and potentially dirty.
1 : Allow continue to run a dynablock that write data in the same page as code. It can gets faster in loading time of some game but can also get unexpected crashes.
2 : Will also, when it detect an HotPage, flag that page as NEVERCLEAN, and so it will not be write protected but Block build from that page will always be tested. It can be faster that way (but some SMC case might not be trapped).

Enable or disable the use of native flags.

0 : Do not use native flags.
1 : Use native flags when possible.

Enable x86 PAUSE emulation, may help the performance of spinlocks.

0 : Ignore x86 PAUSE instruction.
1 : Use YIELD to emulate x86 PAUSE instruction.
2 : Use WFI to emulate x86 PAUSE instruction.
3 : Use SEVL+WFE to emulate x86 PAUSE instruction.

AVX and AVX2 implemented, along with BMI1, BMI2, ADX, FMA, F16C and RDANDR extension!

0 : Disable AVX extension
1 : enable AVX, BMI1, F16C and VAES extension.
2 : All 1 plus enable AVX2, BMI2, FMA, ADX,VPCLMULQDQ and RDRAND.

Optional runtime performance tweaks. May improve demanding games, but compatibility can vary.
When enabled, containers always run in landscape (horizontal) mode and the app returns to portrait automatically when you exit. Turn this off if you want free rotation.
When enabled, the app automatically matches your Android dark/light mode. The Dark Mode checkbox below is disabled while this is on.
Forces the app to use the dark theme. Only works when "Follow Android System Theme" is off.
Caps the GPU VRAM size reported to games. On unified-memory devices (phone RAM shared with GPU) this stops games from allocating more VRAM than the device can handle, avoiding stutters and crashes.
How the VRAM cap size is chosen. Auto picks a safe value based on your device RAM; manual values force a specific cap.
Keeps the Xclipse driver shader pipeline and texture caches between runs, so games compile shaders less often and load faster after the first run.
WinXclipse policy engine: tunes scheduling and memory hints specifically for your SoC (chipset) during the session.
RAM Optimizer Xclipse: aggressively reclaims unused RAM from background apps while a game is running to give the container more memory.
Pins WoW64 (32-bit on 64-bit) translation threads to the performance (big) cores, reducing stutter in 32-bit games.

Applies the new Turbo translator settings without changing the selected preset: larger translated blocks, faster floating-point paths, and relaxed x86 memory/self-modifying-code checks in Box86/Box64 and FEXCore. It can noticeably improve CPU-limited games. Turn it off if a game crashes, hangs, or shows simulation glitches.
Waits for the display on every frame (lowest input latency, slightly lower FPS).
Skips waiting for the display after presenting each frame. Gives more FPS at the cost of possible tearing and higher input latency.
Disables VKD3D timeline semaphores. Use only if a game shows graphical glitches or driver errors on older drivers.
Forces VKD3D-Proton to use shader model 6.6. Can improve performance in some DX12 games; disable if shaders fail to compile.
Disables guest frame pacing for maximum FPS. Android still presents complete compositor frames to prevent physical tearing.
Allows the swapchain to use unlimited images instead of capping them. Lower latency, uses more memory.

Mailbox: tear-free and keeps the newest frame, best default for high FPS. FIFO: tear-free queue synchronized to the display, most compatible but may cap FPS. Immediate: lowest wait and can tear. Relaxed: FIFO normally, but may tear after a missed refresh deadline.

Renders the guest below the selected output resolution, then uses FSR EASU to upscale it. This can improve performance when the GPU is the limit, but may soften fine detail or add shimmer. It only takes effect with the FSR texture filter selected.

Adds a Vulkan post-process sharpening pass. CAS is the lighter default; DLS adds denoise control. It does not increase the rendered resolution and costs some GPU time, so disable it if performance drops or edges look over-sharpened.
Uses the software BCn compression path. Lighter for small WGPs (workgroup sizes) and helps when hardware BCn emulation misbehaves.
Transcodes BCn compressed textures to ETC2. Mutually exclusive with ASTC Transcode.
BCn software path (lighter for small WGPs)
Enables the experimental BCN compatibility layer for this container or shortcut. The optimized Xclipse archive is an optional setting inside this section.
Uses the newer Xclipse-optimized BCN archive and tuning variables. Leave disabled to keep the standard experimental BCN path.

Uses the custom Leegao BCN layer to transcode BCn (BC1-BC7) textures directly into ASTC, a format natively supported by Xclipse RDNA GPUs.

Why it matters: without this, BCn textures are decoded to RGBA8, consuming 4x more video memory.

Benefits: lower VRAM/RAM usage on the unified memory pool and fewer out-of-memory crashes on texture-heavy games, with quality close to the original.

Requires Emulation Type = Compute. Mutually exclusive with ETC2 Transcode.

Wrapper variants provide the Vulkan driver used by DXVK/VKD3D on Exynos Xclipse GPUs. Wrapper-Default is the matched July 13 stack and the recommended starting point for ASTC/ETC2 transcoding. CMOD v1 and v2 remain available for compatibility testing.

Kirimu and GameNative are recommended for BCn texture errors in DirectX 11 and DirectX 12 games.

Enable Experimental BCN Support to expose per-driver BCn controls.

Hides the blinking RAM alert and its high-memory dialog shown when RAM usage crosses the danger threshold.

This only silences the warning — games can still run out of memory on the unified LPDDR pool.

CAS is lighter; DLS adds denoise. Saved for this shortcut/container and applied on its next launch.

Enabling this option will add environmental variables to this container\'s configuration that could impact your ability to launch games. Do not enable this unless you are certain the issue is specific to in-game video playback.

A mandatory update to the system files is needed to ensure compatibility and stability.

Important: After the update, your existing containers WILL will have issues. It is STRONGLY recommended to create a new container and migrate your data (See below)

Migrating Data with Saves Manager:
Use the Saves Manager from the main menu. Register your saves from the old container by navigating and selecting its containing folder, then use the pop-up menu on each registered Save to Transfer (copy) it to the new container. You may also select the AppData directory, and backup an entire container\'s data to another.

Migrating Shortcuts:
While you can duplicate shortcuts via their pop-up menu, it is advised to recreate them manually from inside your new container to prevent issues with mismatched drive paths.

Apex/GLES 3.1 experimental mode. Vulkan is required. It may add latency or visual artifacts; disable it if a game becomes unstable.

Fast uses 1/8-resolution motion search: lowest GPU cost and latency, but more warped edges. Balanced uses 1/4 resolution for a middle ground. Quality uses 1/3-resolution motion search and conservative blending: fewer deformed edges, but higher GPU cost and possible blur or double images.

Experimental GLES 3.1 frame interpolation for Vulkan containers, using the stable GLES Compute path. Low Latency presents real frames immediately and extrapolates generated frames, reducing the normal one-frame delay at the cost of more artifacts. Fixed multipliers are limited to 4x because larger temporal gaps produce severe artifacts. The display refresh rate still limits what is physically visible.

Normal mode keeps a real frame of history for cleaner interpolation. Low Latency presents the newest real frame immediately and extrapolates generated frames: less delay, but more warping, judder and image errors during sudden motion.
